levels.name: Planck referent
levels.known: Planck length = sqrt(hbar G/c^3); Planck time approximately 5.391247e-44 s. Units are computable from measured constants.
levels.unknown: No experimental verification of discrete Planck bubbles, Planck-size vesicles or a microscopic homeostatic compartment; length is not proof of smallest possible distance.
levels.boundary: theoretical dimensional scale, no demonstrated physical shell

levels.name: Quantum / fields
levels.known: Quarks and leptons; electroweak force carriers photon,W,Z; strong-force gluons; Higgs boson; superposition, interference, discrete measurement results, interactions.
levels.unknown: Gravity is not included in the particle Standard Model; origins of dark matter and neutrino masses need further description beyond its simplest form.
levels.boundary: physical states and field interactions, not an isolated membrane

levels.name: Nuclear
levels.known: Quarks and gluons bind to form protons/neutrons; residual strong interaction binds nuclei; proton count sets chemical element; nuclei may undergo radioactive decay, fission or fusion.
levels.unknown: Many-body nuclear calculations have scale-dependent model uncertainties; nuclear forces are not a distinct membrane.
levels.boundary: strongly bound nucleons within an atomic nucleus

levels.name: Atomic
levels.known: Nuclei and electrons form atoms; orbitals, quantized energy levels and electromagnetic interactions determine spectra, ionization and bonding.
levels.unknown: No fixed impenetrable physical atomic shell; electron orbitals are probability distributions and atoms have sizes depending on element/state.
levels.boundary: electronic distributions and nuclear charge, not literal hard spheres

levels.name: Molecular
levels.known: Atoms share or transfer electrons to form chemical bonds, molecules, chemical reactions, membranes and macromolecules. All biology depends on molecular chemistry.
levels.unknown: Molecules do not all share one size or use a single feedback control system.

levels.name: Nucleic (DNA/RNA)
levels.known: Nucleotide polymers DNA and RNA; DNA records genetic sequence, complementary base pairing allows replication; RNA handles gene expression, translation and regulation; proteins perform many functions.
levels.unknown: Nucleic does not mean nuclear (atomic nucleus), not all biology determined by sequence alone; it does not specify a hidden Planck-scale nucleus.
levels.boundary: large molecular information carriers, not membrane-enclosed by default

levels.name: Cellular
levels.known: Selective membranes, vesicles, phagosomes, endocytosis, ion gradients, organelles, metabolism, intracellular signaling, cell reproduction.
levels.unknown: A phagosome is a biologically formed membrane vesicle; no verified equivalence to a Planck-sized bubble.
levels.boundary: physically measured lipid membrane and selectively regulated transport

levels.name: Biological systems / homeostasis
levels.typicalScale: Cells to organisms, no fixed upper size
levels.known: Sensor + reference/set point + control/effector often use negative feedback to maintain acceptable conditions, e.g. temperature and blood glucose; positive feedback supports finite events such as clotting.
levels.unknown: Homeostasis is not a universal physical property of every quantum or nuclear state; 1x1.25 is not a known universal biological constant.
levels.boundary: dynamic regulated non-equilibrium system requiring energy and material exchange
